title: Trump Strips Nearly $1 Billion in Spending, Triggering Battles Over Executive Authority
snippet: President Donald Trump is utilizing a rare 'pocket rescission' maneuver to claw back nearly $1 billion in congressional spending, targeting migrant services, diversity initiatives, and climate programs.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has deployed a rare and fiercely contested executive maneuver to cancel nearly $1 billion in congressionally approved funding, striking targeted blows against migrant support services, diversity initiatives, and foreign climate aid.

The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) characterized the last-minute clawbacks as a necessary campaign to eliminate "harmful and blatantly ideological" government spending. The bulk of the cuts target Health and Human Services (HHS) programs serving refugees and unaccompanied minors, with the White House arguing the expenditures are no longer necessary due to a decrease in border crossings.

Targeting Diversity and Social Programs

The spending purge extends beyond border programs. Among the targeted funds are $70 million for international education programs deemed "woke" by the administration, $10 million from minority business development initiatives, and millions more slated for Department of Justice offices focused on easing racial tensions, HUD housing counseling, and foreign debt relief tied to climate policy. The White House press release notably highlighted that several leadership roles in the affected organizations are held by former officials from the Obama administration.

The 'Pocket Rescission' Controversy

By executing the spending cuts with just five days left in the federal fiscal year—and with the House of Representatives out of session until after the November election—Trump effectively triggered a mechanism known as a "pocket rescission."

Federal statute dictates that Congress must be given a 45-day window to review and vote on any spending cuts proposed by the executive branch. By timing the announcement so late, the administration leaves Congress with no opportunity to act within the fiscal deadline. While the Government Accountability Office (GAO) maintains that pocket rescissions are illegal, the White House asserts the tactic is legally viable, referencing a similar move made by President Jimmy Carter in 1977.

Bipartisan Backlash on Capitol Hill

The aggressive maneuver drew immediate fire from congressional leaders responsible for federal spending, including prominent members of the president's own party.

Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine) forcefully condemned the move, accusing the White House of bypassing constitutional boundaries without warning.

"Not only is the delay itself an impoundment that was not reported to Congress, but also it is a usurpation of Congress’s appropriations powers," Collins stated, pledging to work with lawmakers to address what she termed "illegal actions." She added: "OMB is an agency of the executive branch. It does not get to decide which programs are worth funding."

Senator Patty Murray of Washington, the top Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, termed the maneuver "theft from the American people, plain and simple." Murray called on Senate Republicans to stand firm against executive overreach and reclaim Congress's constitutional authority over the nation's purse strings.

The move marks the administration's second reliance on a pocket rescission, following a $4.9 billion freeze on foreign aid last year that the Supreme Court declined to overturn. However, by applying the maneuver to domestic appropriations, the White House has opened a major new front in the legal and political conflict over the limits of presidential power.
